label: def:local_metric_entropy
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:local_metric_entropy}
    For a set $K$, the $\delta$-packing number is the maximum cardinality $\mathcal{M}(\delta,K)$ of a set $\{\Sigma_1,...,\Sigma_M\} \subseteq K$ such that $\|\Sigma_i - \Sigma_j\|_F \geq \delta$ $\forall i\neq j$. Then for a fixed constant $c>0$ \textbf{the local metric entropy} for the set $K$ is $\mathcal{M}_K^{\operatorname{loc}}(\delta,c) = \sup_{\Sigma \in K} \mathcal{M}(\delta/c, B(\Sigma,\delta) \cap K)$. We refer to $\delta$ as the \textbf{local radius} and c as the \textbf{radius factor}. When the set $K$ is unambiguous, we may drop the $K$ and write $\mathcal{M}^{\operatorname{loc}}(\delta,c)$.
head: environment
name: Local metric entropy

label: def:star_shaped
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:star_shaped}
    A set $K$ is called \textbf{star-shaped with center $k^\star$} if $\exists k^\star \in K$ such that $\forall k \in K$ and $\alpha \in [0,1]$, $\alpha k + (1-\alpha)k^\star \in K$.

title: Definition
body_md:
The minimax estimation under adversarial corruption is given as \[\mathfrak{M}(X) = \inf_{\hat\Sigma} \sup_{\Sigma} \sup_{\mathcal{C}_\varepsilon} \mathbb{E} \| \hat\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_\varepsilon(\tilde{X})) - \Sigma \|_F^2 \]
    where $\mathcal{C}_\varepsilon$ gives the adversarial corruption scheme, $\Sigma$ is the true covariance of $X$ before corruption, and $\hat\Sigma$ is the estimator of $\Sigma$ given the corrupted data $\mathcal{C}_\varepsilon(\tilde{X})$. When the corruption rate is clear we drop the $\varepsilon$ and simply write $\mathcal{C}(\tilde{X})$.

body_md: A single minimax rate is not achieved for this setting - the left and right bounds differ by a factor of $\log^2(1/\varepsilon)$. However, this is a small price to pay. For example, when $\varepsilon = 0$, $\varepsilon^2 = \epsilon^2\log^2(1/\varepsilon)=0$. label: eq:spiked_local_entropy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lemma:spiked_local_entropy}
Let $K^0\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be star-shaped around $0$ and suppose that
\[
    \sup_{x\in K^0}\|x\|_2\leq K_{\max}.
\]
Define
\[
    K^+
    \coloneqq
    \left\{
        I+xx^\top:\ x\in K^0
    \right\}.
\]
Let $\mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote local
metric entropy on $K^0$ with respect to the Euclidean norm, and let
$\mathcal{M}_{K^+}^{\operatorname{loc}}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote local
metric entropy on $K^+$ with respect to the Frobenius norm. Then there
is a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for every $c>0$ and every
$0<\delta\leq K_{\max}^2$,
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal{M}_{K^+}^{\operatorname{loc}}(\delta,c)
    \leq
    2\,
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    \left(
        \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},
        Cc
    \right).
    \label{eq:spiked_local_entropy}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
    \log \mathcal{M}_{K^+}^{\operatorname{loc}}(\delta,c)
    \leq
    \log 2
    +
    \log
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    \left(
        \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},
        Cc
    \right).
    \label{eq:spiked_local_entropy_log}
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Local entropy of rank-one spike classes

label: rem:spiked_local_entropy_fixed_point
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:spiked_local_entropy_fixed_point}
The preceding lemma gives the local, rather than merely global,
entropy comparison needed for the sparse spiked-covariance example.
In particular, if
\[
    \delta_+^\star
    \coloneqq
    \sup\left\{
        \delta>0:
        N\delta^2
        \leq
        \log
        \mathcal{M}_{K^+}^{\operatorname{loc}}(\delta,c)
    \right\},
\]
then, up to changing the fixed radius factor $c$ by a universal
constant, $\delta_+^\star$ is bounded above by the largest $\delta$
satisfying
\[
    N\delta^2
    \leq
    \log 2
    +
    \log
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    \left(
        \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},
        Cc
    \right).
\]
Thus the local entropy of the rank-one covariance class is controlled
by the local Euclidean entropy of the spike class at scale
$\delta/K_{\max}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $K^0$ is star-shaped, $K^+$ is also star shaped around $I$, since if $I + x x^\top$ is in $K^+$, then for any $\alpha \in [0,1]$, $\alpha(I + x x^\top)  + (1-\alpha)I = I + \alpha xx^\top$ is in $K^+$ since $K^0$ is star-shaped around $0$. The identity matrix in the construction implies $\lambda_{\min} \geq 1$. The corruption part of the rate is immediate. We thus show a bound on the local metric entropy to complete the proof.
    Consider an arbitrary point $\Sigma_0 \in K^+$. We need to show that we can form a set of points $\Sigma_1 = I + x_1x_1^\top,...,\Sigma_M = I + x_Mx_M^\top$ in $K^+$ such that for any $\Sigma_0 \in K^+$,  $\exists i$ such that $\|\Sigma_i - \Sigma_0\| \leq \delta^\star$. 

    \textbf{Case 1: $\delta_+^\star \leq K_{\max}^2$. } The conclusion follows by \Cref{lemma:spiked_local_entropy}. 
    \\\textbf{Case 2: $\delta_+^\star > K_{\max}^2$. } 
    Note that 
    \begin{align*}
        \| xx^\top - yy^\top\|_F &\leq \|x(x-y)^\top\|_F + \|(x-y)y^\top\|_F
        \\ &= \|x\|_2\|x-y\|_2 + \|x-y\|_2\|y\|_2
        \\ &\leq 2K_{\max}\|x-y\|_2
    \end{align*}
    and therefore $x \mapsto xx^\top$ is $2K_{\max}$-Lipschitz.
    Fix an arbitrary
    \[
        \Sigma_0=I+x_0x_0^\top\in K^+,
    \]
    and let
    \[
        \{\Sigma_i=I+x_ix_i^\top\}_{i=1}^M
        \subseteq
        B_F(\Sigma_0,\delta)\cap K^+
    \]
    be a $\delta/c$-packing in Frobenius norm.  We will bound $M$
    uniformly over $\Sigma_0$. 
    Now, the Lipschitz inequalty gives that for all $i \neq j$
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\delta}{c} \leq \|\Sigma_i - \Sigma_j\|_F \leq 2K_{\max}\|x_i-x_j\|_2 
    \end{align*}
    and thus the $x_i$ form a $\frac{\delta}{2K_{\max}c}$-packing. Now, since $\delta > K_{\max}^2$ we have that $\frac{\delta}{K_{\max}} > K_{\max}$ and thus for all $x_i \in K^0$ we have $x_i \in B_2\big(0,\frac{\delta}{K_{\max}}\big) \cap K^0$. Furthermore, $0 \in K^0$ by star-shapedness, so we can bound $M \leq \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}\big(\frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},2c\big)$. Taking the supremum over $\Sigma_0$ gives the desired result.

\label{proof:min_max_eigen} Begin with the eigen decomposition of A: 
    \begin{align*}
        A v &= \lambda v
        \\ A^{-1} Av &= \lambda A^{-1}v
        \\ v &= \lambda A^{-1} v 
        \\ \lambda^{-1} v &= A^{-1}v.
    \end{align*}
    Therefore each eigenvalue of $A^{-1}$ is the inverse of an eigenvalue of $A$. Since all eigenvalues are positive this further implies the desired result.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix some $x \in K$ and choose a $\delta/(2c)$ packing $P \subseteq B(x,\delta) \cap K$. Within $P$, further choose a maximal $\delta/c$-separated subset $Q$, and note that $|Q| \leq \mathcal{M}_K^{\textrm{loc}}(\delta,c)$. Further note that since $Q$ is a maximal subset, it is a $\delta/c$-covering of $P$. Cluster $P$ by assigning each point in $P$ to a point in $Q$ less than $\delta/c$ distance from said point. For each $q \in Q$, denote its cluster $R_q \subseteq P$. 
    Now, since $c \geq 2$ we have that $\frac{\delta}{c} \leq \frac{\delta}{2}$ and thus $R_q \subseteq B\big(q,\frac{\delta}{2}\big) \cap K$. Recall that points in $R_q$ are $\delta/(2c)$ separated, and thus $R_q$ contains at most $\mathcal{M}_K^{\textrm{loc}}\big(\frac{\delta}{2},c\big)$ points. Now, over $|Q|$ clusters we have that \[|P| \leq |Q|\mathcal{M}_K^{\textrm{loc}}\bigg(\frac{\delta}{2},c\bigg) \leq \mathcal{M}_K^{\textrm{loc}}(\delta,c)\mathcal{M}_K^{\textrm{loc}}\bigg(\frac{\delta}{2},c\bigg) \leq \mathcal{M}_K^{\textrm{loc}}\bigg(\frac{\delta}{2},c\bigg)^2,\] with the last inequality from monotonicity. Taking the supremum over $P$ and $x$ then taking logs completes the proof.

label: eq:spike_norm_control
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix an arbitrary
\[
    \Sigma_0=I+x_0x_0^\top\in K^+,
\]
and let
\[
    \{\Sigma_i=I+x_ix_i^\top\}_{i=1}^M
    \subseteq
    B_F(\Sigma_0,\delta)\cap K^+
\]
be a $\delta/c$-packing in Frobenius norm.  We will bound $M$
uniformly over $\Sigma_0$.  Write
\[
    a\coloneqq \|x_0\|_2,
    \qquad
    b_i\coloneqq \|x_i\|_2.
\]
For every $i$,
\begin{equation}
    |b_i^2-a^2|
    =
    \left|
        \|x_ix_i^\top\|_F-\|x_0x_0^\top\|_F
    \right|
    \leq
    \|x_ix_i^\top-x_0x_0^\top\|_F
    \leq \delta.
    \label{eq:spike_norm_control}
\end{equation} 
We separate the proof into two cases.

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Case 1: $a^2\leq 2\delta$.}
By \eqref{eq:spike_norm_control},
\[
    b_i^2\leq a^2+\delta\leq 3\delta,
\]
and therefore
\[
    x_i\in B_2(0,\sqrt{3\delta})\cap K^0.
\]
On the other hand, for $i\neq j$,
\begin{align*}
    \frac{\delta}{c}
    &\leq
    \|x_ix_i^\top-x_jx_j^\top\|_F \\
    &=
    \|(x_i-x_j)x_i^\top+x_j(x_i-x_j)^\top\|_F \\
    &\leq
    (b_i+b_j)\|x_i-x_j\|_2 \\
    &\leq
    2\sqrt{3\delta}\,\|x_i-x_j\|_2.
\end{align*}
Hence
\[
    \|x_i-x_j\|_2
    \geq
    \frac{\sqrt{\delta}}{2\sqrt{3}\,c}.
\]
Thus $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^M$ is a
$\sqrt{\delta}/(2\sqrt{3}c)$-packing of
$B_2(0,\sqrt{3\delta})\cap K^0$, and consequently
\[
    M
    \leq
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    (\sqrt{3\delta},6c).
\]
Since $\delta\leq K_{\max}^2$,
\[
    \sqrt{3\delta}
    \geq
    \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}}.
\]
Because $K^0$ is star-shaped, its local metric entropy is
non-increasing in the local radius.  Therefore
\begin{equation}
    M
    \leq
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    \left(
        \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},
        6c
    \right).
    \label{eq:small_spike_case}
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Case 2: $a^2>2\delta$.}
In this case \eqref{eq:spike_norm_control} gives
\begin{equation}
    \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}
    \leq b_i
    \leq
    \sqrt{\frac32}\,a
    \qquad
    \text{for every }i.
    \label{eq:bi_comparable_a}
\end{equation}
For each $i$, choose $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ so that
$s_i\langle x_i,x_0\rangle\geq 0$.  We claim that
\begin{equation}
    \|x_i-s_ix_0\|_2
    \leq
    \frac{2\delta}{a}.
    \label{eq:local_inverse_rank_one}
\end{equation}
To see this, set
\[
    t_i
    \coloneqq
    \frac{|\langle x_i,x_0\rangle|}{ab_i}
    \in[0,1].
\]
The identity
\begin{align*}
    \|x_ix_i^\top-x_0x_0^\top\|_F^2
    &=
    b_i^4+a^4-2\langle x_i,x_0\rangle^2 \\
    &=
    (b_i^2-a^2)^2
    +
    2a^2b_i^2(1-t_i^2)
\end{align*}
and the fact that the left-hand side is at most $\delta^2$ implies
\[
    2a^2b_i^2(1-t_i^2)\leq \delta^2.
\]
Moreover,
\[
    |b_i-a|
    =
    \frac{|b_i^2-a^2|}{a+b_i}
    \leq
    \frac{\delta}{a}.
\]
Therefore, using $1-t_i\leq 1-t_i^2$ and
$b_i\geq a/\sqrt{2}$,
\begin{align*}
    \|x_i-s_ix_0\|_2^2
    &=
    (b_i-a)^2+2ab_i(1-t_i) \\
    &\leq
    \frac{\delta^2}{a^2}
    +
    2ab_i(1-t_i^2) \\
    &\leq
    \frac{\delta^2}{a^2}
    +
    \frac{\delta^2}{ab_i} \\
    &\leq
    (1+\sqrt{2})\frac{\delta^2}{a^2}
    <
    \frac{4\delta^2}{a^2},
\end{align*}
which proves \eqref{eq:local_inverse_rank_one}.

Partition the packing indices according to the sign $s_i$:
\[
    I_+\coloneqq\{i:s_i=1\},
    \qquad
    I_-\coloneqq\{i:s_i=-1\}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:local_inverse_rank_one},
\[
    \{x_i:i\in I_+\}
    \subseteq
    B_2\left(x_0,\frac{2\delta}{a}\right)\cap K^0.
\]
If $I_-\neq\varnothing$, choose any $i_0\in I_-$ and put
$z=x_{i_0}\in K^0$.  Then, again by
\eqref{eq:local_inverse_rank_one},
\[
    \{x_i:i\in I_-\}
    \subseteq
    B_2\left(z,\frac{4\delta}{a}\right)\cap K^0.
\]
Thus both sign classes are contained in a Euclidean ball, centered
at a point of $K^0$, of radius at most $4\delta/a$.

It remains to control their packing separation.  For $i\neq j$,
\begin{align*}
    \frac{\delta}{c}
    &\leq
    \|x_ix_i^\top-x_jx_j^\top\|_F \\
    &\leq
    (b_i+b_j)\|x_i-x_j\|_2 \\
    &\leq
    \sqrt{6}\,a\,\|x_i-x_j\|_2,
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from
\eqref{eq:bi_comparable_a}.  Hence
\[
    \|x_i-x_j\|_2
    \geq
    \frac{\delta}{\sqrt{6}\,ca}
    =
    \frac{4\delta/a}{4\sqrt{6}\,c}.
\]
It follows that each sign class has cardinality at most
\[
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    \left(
        \frac{4\delta}{a},
        4\sqrt{6}\,c
    \right).
\]
Since $a\leq K_{\max}$,
\[
    \frac{4\delta}{a}
    \geq
    \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},
\]
so the monotonicity of local metric entropy again yields
\begin{equation}
    M
    \leq
    2\,
    \mathcal{M}_{K^0}^{\operatorname{loc}}
    \left(
        \frac{\delta}{K_{\max}},
        4\sqrt{6}\,c
    \right).
    \label{eq:large_spike_case}
\end{equation}

Combining \eqref{eq:small_spike_case} and
\eqref{eq:large_spike_case}, and taking for example $C=10$,
gives \eqref{eq:spiked_local_entropy}.  Since the bound is uniform
over $\Sigma_0\in K^+$, taking the supremum over the local center
completes the proof.
head: environment
